source_evidence.observation: The standing problem is Ax = b with nonsingular A in R^(n x n) and nonzero b in R^n; x denotes the exact solution. (PDF p. 1, anchor: equation (1.1))

source_evidence.anchor: Section 2, floating-point notation and error definitions
source_evidence.observation: The paper uses the standard floating-point model, hats for computed quantities, gamma_k = ku/(1-ku), generic low-degree polynomials c(n,k), and the symbols lesssim and approximately-equal when negligible second-order terms are dropped. It defines the relative 2-norm forward error, normwise backward error, 2-norm, Frobenius norm, and kappa_F. (PDF p. 4, anchor: Section 2 notation and definitions)

The modular operation model bounds the computed matrix-basis product in Frobenius norm, the computed preconditioned right-hand side in 2-norm, and a columnwise backward error for the least-squares solve. (PDF p. 6, anchor: conditions (3.1)-(3.3))

The computed solution or correction has a matrix-vector-product error bounded by epsilon_x ||Z_k||_F ||y_hat_k||_2; Z_k must not be numerically rank deficient at that accuracy; and all four modular accuracy parameters must be nonnegative and much less than one. (PDF p. 7, anchor: conditions (3.4)-(3.6))

The key dimension is the first k <= n for which the augmented matrix [b_tilde phi, A_tilde Z_k] is nearly rank deficient for every phi > 0 when k <= n-1, while A_tilde Z_k remains numerically full rank; at k = n only the latter condition is required. (PDF p. 8, anchor: conditions (3.7)-(3.8))

Restarted MOD-GMRES forms an outer residual, solves a correction system with a possibly restart-dependent basis and preconditioner, and updates the iterate. Its residual model is r_hat_i = b - A x_hat_i + Delta r_i with a normwise bound. (PDF p. 16, anchor: Algorithm 2 and equation (4.1))

Theorem 4.1 assumes the modular conditions at every restart, small residual and update errors, and ||x_hat_i||_2 lesssim ||x_hat_(i+1)||_2 lesssim ||x||_2. It gives a restart-wise forward-error contraction factor Lambda_1^(i) and the floor c(n,k) epsilon_r kappa_F(A) + epsilon_u. (PDF p. 17, anchor: Theorem 4.1 and equations (4.2)-(4.7))

Independently, Theorem 4.1 imposes an additional numerical-rank condition and Lambda_2^(i) much less than one, then gives restart-wise backward-error contraction to the floor c(n,k) epsilon_r + epsilon_u. (PDF p. 18, anchor: equations (4.8)-(4.11))

For fully stored MGS-GMRES in unit roundoff u, sigma_min(A) much greater than u||A||_F guarantees a key iteration k <= n and normwise backward error lesssim c(n,k)u. The proof identifies the MGS least-squares accuracy through equation (5.13). (PDF p. 27, anchor: Theorem 5.2 and equation (5.13))

At the selected MGS key iteration the stored basis satisfies kappa_2(V_hat_k) <= 4/3, sigma_min(V_hat_k)^(-1) <= 4/3, and sigma_max(V_hat_k) <= 4/3; loss of orthogonality of V_hat_(k+1) supplies the near-rank-deficiency certificate for [b phi, C_hat_k]. (PDF p. 28, anchor: equations (5.15)-(5.16))

The MGS proof transfers the near-rank-deficiency certificate to [b phi, A V_hat_k] and proves sigma_min(A V_hat_k) >= (3/4)sigma_min(A), establishing the key-dimension conditions. (PDF p. 29, anchor: equations (5.17)-(5.18))

Mixed precision GMRES is unpreconditioned restarted MGS-GMRES with fully stored MGS-Arnoldi bases; residuals and updates are computed in precision u_high and lines 4-7 of Algorithm 2 in precision u_low. Under Lambda = c(n,k)u_low kappa_F(A) much less than one, both errors contract to the two bounds in (6.18). Equations (6.19)-(6.20) give componentwise high-precision residual and update models. (PDF p. 40, anchor: Theorem 6.3 and equations (6.17)-(6.20))

source_evidence.anchor: low-precision cast, equations (6.21), and final factor bound
source_evidence.observation: The high-precision residual is cast to low precision with relative 2-norm error at most u_low. For every restart i there is a key dimension k_i; the specialized quantity xi_1^(i) is lesssim c(n,k)u_low, and max(Lambda_1^(i), Lambda_2^(i)) <= Lambda. (PDF p. 41, anchor: residual-cast display, equation (6.21), and final proof display)

binders: A in R^(n x n) is nonsingular, 0 != b in R^n, and x = A^(-1)b is the exact solution. (PDF p. 1, anchor: equation (1.1))
u_high and u_low are the unit roundoffs used respectively for the residual/update and all remaining mixed-precision GMRES operations. (PDF p. 40, anchor: Theorem 6.3)

For each outer restart i >= 0, x_hat_i, r_hat_i, d_hat_i, and the associated errors are vectors in R^n, while the fully stored basis V_hat_(k_i)^(i) has size n x k_i with a key dimension k_i <= n. (PDF p. 16, anchor: Algorithm 2; PDF p. 41, anchor: key-iteration paragraph)

The theorem writes c(n,k) and Lambda using a generic basis dimension k, while the proof quantifies restart-dependent dimensions as: for every i >= 0, there exists k_i <= n. (PDF p. 40, anchor: equations (6.17)-(6.18); PDF p. 41, anchor: key-iteration paragraph)
hypotheses: Explicit theorem hypothesis: Lambda = c(n,k) u_low kappa_F(A) << 1. (PDF p. 40, anchor: Theorem 6.3 and equation (6.17))

Explicit algorithm hypothesis: M_L^(i) = I and Z_(k_i)^(i) = V_hat_(k_i)^(i), where V_hat_(k_i)^(i) is the fully formed and stored Krylov basis computed by MGS Arnoldi at restart i. (PDF p. 40, anchor: opening paragraph of Section 6.3)

Explicit precision split: the standard matrix-vector residual and vector update are computed in high precision; the correction-system operations corresponding to lines 4-7 of Algorithm 2 are MGS-GMRES operations computed in low precision. (PDF p. 40, anchor: opening paragraph of Section 6.3 and proof after (6.20))

Inherited modular hypotheses at every restart: the product, low-precision right-hand side, least-squares solution, and correction update satisfy conditions (3.1)-(3.6), and a key dimension satisfies conditions (3.7)-(3.8). (PDF pp. 6-8, anchors: conditions (3.1)-(3.8); PDF p. 40, anchor: opening of Theorem 6.3 proof)

Inherited MGS certificate: sigma_min(A) >> u_low ||A||_F gives a key dimension k_i <= n at every restart; the proof states that (6.17) guarantees this inequality. (PDF p. 27, anchor: Theorem 5.2; PDF p. 41, anchor: paragraph preceding (6.21))

Inherited Theorem 4.1 hypotheses include ||x_hat_i||_2 lesssim ||x_hat_(i+1)||_2 lesssim ||x||_2, small epsilon_r and epsilon_u, and, for backward contraction, sigma_min(A Z_(k_i)^(i)) >> epsilon_x^(i)||A||_F||Z_(k_i)^(i)||_F. (PDF pp. 17-18, anchor: Theorem 4.1 before (4.4) and before (4.8))
conclusions: At each outer restart, the backward and forward errors reduce by a factor described in Theorem 6.3 as '(at least) Lambda' until they satisfy the attainable bounds in (6.18). (PDF p. 40, anchor: Theorem 6.3 and equations (6.17)-(6.18))
More precisely in the proof, the separate factors from Theorem 4.1 satisfy max(Lambda_1^(i), Lambda_2^(i)) <= Lambda = c(n,k)u_low kappa_F(A). (PDF p. 41, anchor: final factor-bound display)
The attainable normwise backward error satisfies ||b-A x_hat||_2/(||b||_2+||A||_F||x_hat||_2) lesssim c(n,k)u_high. (PDF p. 40, anchor: equation (6.18), first bound)
The attainable relative forward error satisfies ||x_hat-x||_2/||x||_2 lesssim c(n,k)u_high kappa_F(A). (PDF p. 40, anchor: equation (6.18), second bound)
definitions_and_conventions: A hat denotes a computed quantity and fl denotes floating-point evaluation. (PDF p. 4, anchor: first paragraph of Section 2)

gamma_q = q u/(1-q u); a superscript on gamma selects the correspondingly subscripted unit roundoff, so gamma_n^high = n u_high/(1-nu_high). A decorated gamma hides a modest multiplicative constant in its index. (PDF p. 4, anchor: gamma notation)

c(n,k) denotes generic constants gathered into polynomials in n and k of low degree; precise polynomial coefficients are not tracked consistently. (PDF p. 4, anchor: paragraph defining c(n,k); PDF p. 40, anchor: sentence after (6.18))

The key dimension is the first k <= n meeting the near-rank-deficiency and numerical-full-rank conditions (3.7)-(3.8); if k = n, only (3.8) is required. (PDF p. 8, anchor: Section 3.2 and conditions (3.7)-(3.8))

For MGS, if orthogonality is never fully lost, k = n supplies the key dimension; otherwise the key dimension is the first k for which kappa_2(V_hat_(k+1)) > 4/3, while V_hat_k still satisfies (5.15). (PDF pp. 28-29, anchor: discussion surrounding equations (5.15)-(5.18))
implicit_context: The unqualified word 'iteration' in Theorem 6.3 refers, through Algorithm 2 and Theorem 4.1, to an outer restart iteration i, not to each inner Arnoldi step. (PDF p. 16, anchor: Algorithm 2; PDF pp. 17-18, anchor: Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 41, anchor: factor-bound display)

The analysis allows an unbounded, rather than a fixed prescribed, number of Arnoldi iterations at each restart; the key-dimension proof nevertheless selects a finite k_i <= n. (PDF p. 40, anchor: paragraph immediately before Theorem 6.3; PDF p. 41, anchor: key-iteration paragraph)

Theorem 6.3 obtains both conclusions by specializing the independently stated forward and backward parts of Theorem 4.1 and bounding both contraction factors by the same Lambda. (PDF pp. 17-18, anchor: Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 41, anchor: final factor-bound display)

The symbol x_hat in (6.18) denotes a computed iterate once the corresponding error has reached its attainable regime; (6.18) does not attach a specific restart index to it. (PDF p. 40, anchor: equation (6.18))
statement.algorithm_linkage: The selected result concerns restarted, unpreconditioned, mixed-precision MGS-GMRES as Algorithm 2: at restart i it computes r_hat_i in high precision, casts that residual to low precision, applies fully stored MGS-GMRES in low precision to A d_i = r_hat_i using Z_(k_i)^(i) = V_hat_(k_i)^(i), and performs x_hat_(i+1) = x_hat_i + d_hat_i in high precision. (PDF p. 16, anchor: Algorithm 2; PDF pp. 40-41, anchor: Section 6.3 algorithm description and residual-cast display)
numerical_model: The general convention is the standard floating-point model. (PDF p. 4, anchor: first paragraph of Section 2)
High-precision residual model: r_hat_i = b - A x_hat_i + Delta r_i with componentwise |Delta r_i| <= gamma_n^high (|b| + |A||x_hat_i|). (PDF p. 40, anchor: equation (6.19))
High-precision update model: x_hat_(i+1) = x_hat_i + d_hat_i + Delta x_i with componentwise |Delta x_i| <= u_high |x_hat_(i+1)|. (PDF p. 40, anchor: equation (6.20))

Low-precision cast model: r_hat_i' = fl_low(r_hat_i) = r_hat_i + Delta_b^(i), with ||Delta_b^(i)||_2 <= u_low ||r_hat_i||_2, giving epsilon_b^(i) = u_low. (PDF p. 41, anchor: residual-cast display and following sentence)

The inherited MGS specialization uses low-precision analogues of epsilon_c = k^(1/2) gamma_tilde_n ||A||_F/||A V_hat_k||_F, epsilon_ls = gamma_tilde_(n(k+1)), and epsilon_x = gamma_n; together with the cast error, these yield xi_1^(i) lesssim c(n,k)u_low. (PDF p. 27, anchor: Theorem 5.2 proof and equation (5.13); PDF p. 41, anchor: equation (6.21))

The modular product, least-squares, and correction errors are normwise or columnwise bounds, while the specialized high-precision residual and update bounds in (6.19)-(6.20) are componentwise. (PDF pp. 6-7, anchor: conditions (3.1)-(3.4); PDF p. 40, anchor: equations (6.19)-(6.20))
error_notions: The forward error is the relative 2-norm error ||x_hat-x||_2/||x||_2, comparing a computed approximation with the exact solution. (PDF p. 4, anchor: forward-error definition)

The normwise backward error is ||b-Ax_hat||_2/(||A||_F||x_hat||_2+||b||_2), equivalent to the smallest common relative Frobenius/2-norm perturbation size for A and b. (PDF p. 4, anchor: normwise backward-error definition)

The conclusions are attainable-error floors reached after contraction, not claims that every intermediate iterate already satisfies the floor. (PDF p. 40, anchor: text between equations (6.17) and (6.18))
norms: Vector errors use the Euclidean 2-norm. Matrix backward perturbations and matrix condition numbers in the selected theorem use the Frobenius norm. (PDF p. 4, anchor: norm and error definitions)
For nonsingular A, kappa_F(A) = ||A^(-1)||_F ||A||_F. (PDF p. 4, anchor: condition-number definition)
The MGS basis certificate uses the spectral condition number kappa_2 and singular values, specifically the threshold 4/3 in (5.15). (PDF p. 28, anchor: equation (5.15))
constants_and_indexing: Outer restarts are indexed by i >= 0; the next iterate is i+1, and each restart may have its own basis size and key dimension k_i. (PDF p. 16, anchor: Algorithm 2; PDF p. 41, anchor: key-iteration paragraph)
The MGS least-squares perturbation bound is columnwise for j <= k+1, reflecting the augmented right-hand-side-plus-k-columns matrix. (PDF p. 27, anchor: equation (5.13))

The basis used at key dimension k remains well conditioned with the explicit constants kappa_2(V_hat_k) <= 4/3, sigma_min(V_hat_k)^(-1) <= 4/3, and sigma_max(V_hat_k) <= 4/3. (PDF p. 28, anchor: equation (5.15))
The contraction parameter contains no displayed additive high-precision term: Lambda is c(n,k)u_low kappa_F(A), whereas the two floors depend on u_high. (PDF p. 40, anchor: equations (6.17)-(6.18))
higher_order_terms: The relation lesssim and the paper's approximately-equal notation explicitly drop negligible second-order terms. (PDF p. 4, anchor: notation paragraph defining lesssim and approximately-equal)
Equation (6.18) therefore gives approximate upper bounds rather than exact inequalities with stated remainder terms. (PDF p. 40, anchor: equation (6.18); PDF p. 4, anchor: notation convention)
No explicit big-O remainder or quantified second-order term is retained in Theorem 6.3. (PDF p. 40, anchor: Theorem 6.3 and equations (6.17)-(6.18))
exceptional_values: The standing system excludes singular A and zero b. (PDF p. 1, anchor: equation (1.1))

The passage does not explicitly discuss overflow, underflow, subnormal arithmetic, NaNs, infinities, or hardware exceptions; it only invokes the standard floating-point model. (PDF p. 4, anchor: first paragraph of Section 2)

The theorem does not separately discuss an exactly zero residual at a later restart or a breakdown branch; its proof assumes the correction-system framework until convergence. (PDF p. 16, anchor: Algorithm 2; PDF pp. 40-41, anchor: Theorem 6.3 proof)

undebatable_constraints: The result is about unpreconditioned restarted MGS-GMRES with fully stored MGS-Arnoldi bases, not arbitrary GMRES or a preconditioned variant. (PDF p. 40, anchor: opening paragraph of Section 6.3)
Residual and update operations use u_high; all correction-system operations use u_low. (PDF p. 40, anchor: Theorem 6.3)
The sole displayed convergence condition in Theorem 6.3 is c(n,k)u_low kappa_F(A) << 1. (PDF p. 40, anchor: equation (6.17))
Both backward and forward errors contract; neither half of the two-part conclusion may be omitted. (PDF p. 40, anchor: sentence preceding equation (6.18))
The backward floor is c(n,k)u_high in the paper's lesssim sense and uses the denominator ||b||_2+||A||_F||x_hat||_2. (PDF p. 40, anchor: equation (6.18), first bound)
The forward floor is c(n,k)u_high kappa_F(A) in the paper's lesssim sense and uses relative 2-norm error. (PDF p. 40, anchor: equation (6.18), second bound)
The proof bounds both actual restart-wise contraction factors above by Lambda. (PDF p. 41, anchor: final factor-bound display)
For every restart i, the proof invokes a finite key dimension k_i <= n supplied by the MGS analysis. (PDF p. 41, anchor: paragraph preceding equation (6.21))
The residual cast into low precision contributes epsilon_b^(i) = u_low and cannot be treated as exact. (PDF p. 41, anchor: residual-cast display)
The lesssim bounds suppress negligible second-order terms and do not state exact remainder constants. (PDF p. 4, anchor: notation convention; PDF p. 40, anchor: equation (6.18))

ambiguities.issue: The function c(n,k) is not a fixed, explicitly specified polynomial and may represent different low-degree polynomials at different occurrences.
ambiguities.evidence: The notation section says precise values are not always tracked, and the proof says the common factor bound holds 'for a given c(n,k)'. (PDF p. 4, anchor: paragraph defining c(n,k); PDF p. 41, anchor: final factor-bound paragraph)
ambiguities.impact: Lambda and the attainable floors cannot be interpreted as numerical formulas with a uniquely determined constant.

ambiguities.issue: The relations <<, >>, and lesssim are qualitative rather than explicit threshold inequalities.
ambiguities.evidence: The notation section defines >> through informal 'much greater than' language and defines lesssim by dropping negligible second-order terms; Theorem 6.3 uses << and lesssim. (PDF p. 4, anchor: notation conventions; PDF p. 40, anchor: equations (6.17)-(6.18))
ambiguities.impact: An exact formal statement must either preserve these relations abstractly or choose additional quantitative constants and remainder bounds not supplied by the paper.

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 6.3 says reduction is by a factor '(at least) Lambda', while its proof establishes actual factors Lambda_1^(i) and Lambda_2^(i) bounded above by Lambda.
ambiguities.evidence: The wording appears immediately before (6.18), and the proof concludes max(Lambda_1^(i),Lambda_2^(i)) <= Lambda. (PDF p. 40, anchor: Theorem 6.3 after (6.17); PDF p. 41, anchor: final factor-bound display)
ambiguities.impact: The defensible algebraic reading is an error multiplier no larger than Lambda, but the theorem does not write a direct recurrence for either normalized error.

ambiguities.issue: The theorem calls the precisions 'high' and 'low' but does not explicitly state u_high < u_low.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 6.3 only assigns the two unit roundoffs to operation groups; no inequality between them is displayed. (PDF p. 40, anchor: Theorem 6.3 opening sentence)
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract should not add an ordering between the unit roundoffs unless it is treated as part of the terminology rather than an explicit hypothesis.

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 6.3 does not restate every hypothesis of the cross-referenced Theorem 4.1.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 4.1 assumes iterate-norm comparability, 0 <= epsilon_r,epsilon_u << 1, and an additional numerical-rank condition for backward contraction, while the opening of the proof of Theorem 6.3 mentions only conditions (4.1)-(4.3) and (3.1)-(3.8). (PDF pp. 17-18, anchor: Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 40, anchor: opening of Theorem 6.3 proof)
ambiguities.impact: These are inherited proof obligations, but the source does not clearly distinguish which are automatic consequences of (6.17) and which remain standing assumptions.

ambiguities.issue: The symbol k in c(n,k) is not explicitly tied to the restart-dependent k_i in the theorem statement.
ambiguities.evidence: Equations (6.17)-(6.18) use k, while the proof later states that for every i there exists a key iteration k_i. (PDF p. 40, anchor: equations (6.17)-(6.18); PDF p. 41, anchor: key-iteration paragraph)
ambiguities.impact: For varying restart lengths, the source does not specify whether one should use each k_i, their maximum, or a uniform polynomial bound.

ambiguities.issue: No initial iterate or quantitative number of restarts needed to reach the floors is specified.
ambiguities.evidence: Algorithm 2 merely says to initialize x_0, and Section 6.3 says accuracy is obtained after a suitable number of restarts. (PDF p. 16, anchor: Algorithm 2 line 1; PDF p. 40, anchor: opening paragraph of Section 6.3)
ambiguities.impact: The theorem is an attainable-accuracy and contraction statement, not an iteration-complexity bound from a prescribed starting point.

ambiguities.issue: Exceptional floating-point behavior and exact-breakdown cases are not modeled explicitly.
ambiguities.evidence: Only the standard floating-point model is invoked, and neither Theorem 6.3 nor its proof states overflow, underflow, NaN, infinity, or zero-residual handling assumptions. (PDF p. 4, anchor: floating-point convention; PDF pp. 40-41, anchor: Theorem 6.3 and proof)
ambiguities.impact: A machine-level formalization would require additional exceptional-value assumptions not present in the passage.

contract_plain_english: For a nonsingular real system Ax=b, run unpreconditioned restarted GMRES with a fully stored MGS-Arnoldi basis at each restart. Compute each outer residual and iterate update in precision u_high, cast the residual to low precision, and compute the MGS-GMRES correction in precision u_low. If the generic low-degree bound Lambda=c(n,k)u_low kappa_F(A) is much less than one, then at every outer restart the actual forward- and backward-error contraction factors are bounded by Lambda. The process contracts until the normwise backward error is lesssim c(n,k)u_high and the relative 2-norm forward error is lesssim c(n,k)u_high kappa_F(A). These are approximate attainable bounds with negligible second-order terms omitted, and the proof inherits the key-dimension and iterate-size assumptions of Theorems 5.2 and 4.1. (PDF pp. 40-41, anchor: Theorem 6.3 and equations (6.17)-(6.21); PDF pp. 17-18, anchor: Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 4, anchor: notation conventions)
